author: tcoratger
content:
Hey,

As you can see, this channel has just been moved under the post-quantum umbrella. As you’ve likely noticed over the past few days or weeks, there is significant momentum building around the PQ for Ethereum narrative—driven not only by the threat of quantum computers, which appears increasingly imminent, but also by a new, potentially more immediate threat: AI.

All of this suggests we may need to reconsider parts of our roadmap to accelerate Ethereum’s transition to a post-quantum state across all network layers: execution, consensus, and data availability (though the latter is arguably less urgent than the first two, at least in the context of Ethereum’s core operations).

To ensure clear communication among all stakeholders—researchers, developers, the community, and so on—we’ve created this dedicated post-quantum section to house all related discussions. This includes EIPs, specifications, implementation, formal verification, research, and more. Previously, these discussions were scattered across various other channels; we felt now was the right time to bring everything together in one place so that everyone can benefit from all the information and take part in the discussions.

To get things started, in addition to this general communication channel (where we can discuss meta-level questions), we have set up three sub-channels, each focused on a key area that needs to be addressed:
- `pq-cl`: Covers the transition of the consensus layer (e.g., the XMSS signature scheme, public key registration for validators, the shift from BLS to XMSS, and signature aggregation via SNARKs using leanVM).
- `pq-el`: Covers the transition of the execution layer (e.g., the SPHINCS signature scheme, mempool/networking considerations, and signature aggregation via leanVM).
- `pq-networking`: Dedicated to networking, as this topic is relevant to everything we do across all layers.

content: This afternoon, I will post a message for each subgroup to provide a bit more context, along with some links and resources that may be useful for each workspace.
